concepts.decision: Collect evidence tied to the objective and protect its integrity before interpreting a pass/fail result.
concepts.definition: Time-stamped artifacts that substantiate what was attempted, observed, decided, and achieved in a test.
concepts.failureExample: A verbal claim that “failover worked” cannot establish recovery time, data state, or authorization.
concepts.label: Test Evidence

concepts.decision: Record facts and context first; do not label it a failure until the expected condition and evidence are compared.
concepts.definition: A recorder’s factual note about behavior, timing, deviation, or condition during an exercise.
concepts.failureExample: Treating an uncorroborated impression as a finding can send remediation at the wrong problem.
concepts.label: Exercise Observation

concepts.decision: Classify it by capability, documentation, process, or ownership and link it to the challenged recovery assumption.
concepts.definition: A validated gap between an expected recovery condition and observed evidence, with stated impact and confidence.
concepts.failureExample: A finding with no stated consequence cannot be prioritized or accepted as risk.
concepts.label: DR Finding

concepts.decision: Assign action only after the finding is understood; record dependencies and an explicit risk disposition if it cannot be completed.
concepts.definition: A specific change assigned to an accountable owner to address a validated finding, with due date and acceptance evidence.
concepts.failureExample: “Update DR plan” without owner or acceptance test creates an untrackable promise.
concepts.label: Corrective Action

concepts.decision: Derive lessons from supported findings across the exercise; avoid turning blame or a single anecdote into a general rule.
concepts.definition: A reusable conclusion that explains why the observed result occurred and changes future recovery decisions or capability.
concepts.failureExample: A blame-focused lesson discourages reporting and leaves the system condition unchanged.
concepts.label: Lessons Learned

concepts.decision: Update the plan through change control after a verified need; identify which plan element and dependency changed.
concepts.definition: Controlled updating of contacts, assumptions, diagrams, procedures, and commitments as conditions change.
concepts.failureExample: A stale contact list can make an otherwise sound recovery design unusable during activation.
concepts.label: Plan Maintenance

concepts.decision: Retest the failed path and predefined acceptance evidence, not merely a different easy scenario.
concepts.definition: A proportionate repeat exercise that demonstrates the specific corrected condition now works.
concepts.failureExample: Closing a ticket after editing a document without exercising the changed handoff leaves the capability unverified.
concepts.label: Retest

concepts.decision: Communicate status with scope and limitations to the appropriate decision makers; never equate schedule completion with readiness.
concepts.definition: An accurate statement of what scope/objectives passed, failed, were untested, or remain at risk.
concepts.failureExample: A blanket “passed” report can cause leaders to accept recovery risk they were never shown.
concepts.label: Test Status

concepts.decision: Use counsel/compliance-approved triggers, audience, timing, and facts; do not invent a reporting duty from the exercise alone.
concepts.definition: A governed disclosure to a regulator about exercise status or material gaps when a legal, contractual, or supervisory obligation applies.
concepts.failureExample: An unapproved disclosure can be inaccurate or omit required facts; silence can breach an applicable duty.
concepts.label: Regulator Communication

concepts.decision: Assess readiness from objective evidence and unresolved risk, not from the existence of a plan or a single exercise.
concepts.definition: The supported confidence that people, plans, dependencies, and capability can meet stated recovery needs.
concepts.failureExample: Declaring readiness while a key dependency remains untested creates false assurance.
concepts.label: Recovery Readiness

misconceptions.claim: Updating the DR document closes a failed exercise finding.
misconceptions.correction: A document update is only closure when the underlying capability, ownership, or decision has been made executable and retested.

misconceptions.claim: Lessons learned are informal notes for the next exercise.
misconceptions.correction: Material lessons need owners, deadlines, evidence, change control, and risk disposition.

outcome: Given DR exercise evidence, classify findings, assign corrective action, communicate status, update the plan, and define a retest that demonstrates closure.

sections.body: Capture the objective, planned condition, observed condition, evidence, timing, participants, deviation, consequence, and confidence. Separate a documentation issue from a capability failure and a process or ownership failure; each requires different remediation. Classify findings by impact and urgency, link them to the recovery assumption they challenge, and communicate test status to the right stakeholders, including regulators or customers when required. Do not claim a plan passed simply because the exercise completed on schedule.
keyPoints: Evidence should support both what happened and what the exercise could not test.
A finding needs a consequence or risk statement, not just a description of inconvenience.
Test status communications must distinguish exercise success, capability success, and unresolved risk.
sections.title: Turn observations into defensible findings

sections.body: Assign each material finding an accountable owner, corrective action, due date, dependency, acceptance evidence, and risk disposition. Update contacts, diagrams, procedures, assumptions, supplier commitments, training, and recovery configuration under change control. A retest should target the failed condition, use a proportionate form, and define evidence that the action closed the gap rather than merely changing a document. Track overdue or accepted exceptions and schedule the next exercise when system, supplier, threat, or business conditions change.
keyPoints: Plan maintenance is a controlled change with version, approval, and communication evidence.
Closure means the intended capability or decision works, not that an action was marked complete.
Retest scope should be large enough to verify the fix and small enough to isolate what changed.
sections.title: Maintain the plan and prove closure

options.feedback: Changed fact: A full-interruption exercise was stopped safely, but the recovery team did not test customer communications or regulator notification. Why this answer fails: “Reuse the original conclusion because the overall control family is unchanged” does not account for that changed condition. Corrected consequence: Classify the issue as a people and communication capability gap, assign a primary and alternate owner, test the approved channels, update the plan version, and retest contact activation. Repair target: Decision recomputed — Record the exercise as partially successful, assign communication and regulatory actions, update the scope and contact plan, and schedule a targeted retest. A safe stop is valuable evidence but does not prove the untested stakeholder path.
options.label: Reuse the original conclusion because the overall control family is unchanged

options.feedback: Changed fact: A full-interruption exercise was stopped safely, but the recovery team did not test customer communications or regulator notification. Why this answer fails: “Bypass the normal owner and apply a permanent broad restriction immediately” does not account for that changed condition. Corrected consequence: Classify the issue as a people and communication capability gap, assign a primary and alternate owner, test the approved channels, update the plan version, and retest contact activation. Repair target: Changed outcome verified — The decision remains provisional until the changed dependency, enforcement result, and accountable evidence are verified.
options.label: Bypass the normal owner and apply a permanent broad restriction immediately
